issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a Rideable interface (with method messageOnRide()), but the solution repository uses a different interface name (Mountable) for the same purpose and leaves Rideable.java essentially empty. This name/type mismatch between 'Rideable' and 'Mountable' is structural and will confuse students: template/Main and the UML/spec expect Rideable, whereas the solution's classes implement Mountable. Tests or student code referencing Rideable will not match the solution layout.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Either (a) rename Mountable.java to Rideable.java and have it declare String messageOnRide(), updating Pig.java and Seal.java to implement Rideable; or (b) update the problem statement and template to use Mountable everywhere. Ensure Rideable.java in the solution is removed or contains the correct interface so student code, template, and tests consistently reference the same interface name.

issues.description: The exercise and template refer to the rideable interface as 'Rideable' (problem statement and template Main.java), but the solution code uses the name 'Mountable' for the same concept (interface implemented by Pig and Seal). Additionally, solution's Rideable.java is empty. This naming mismatch (Rideable vs Mountable) creates confusion mapping the problem requirements to the solution and template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the rideable interface name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) rename Mountable.java and its usages to Rideable (update class declarations in Pig.java and Seal.java to implement Rideable) and remove/replace the empty Rideable.java, or (B) change the problem statement and template references to use Mountable. Prefer (A) to match the exercise wording and template expectations.
